records.title: Complete the 5:30am morning routine before 7am
records.outcome: The routine done on at least 26 days this month — about 85%
records.why: To develop spiritual maturity, physical fitness, effective communication, knowledge, self-discipline and purposeful living through consistent daily habits. Eighty-five minutes of activity between 5:30 and 7:00, with five minutes for transitions.

steps.text: Up at 5:30 — kit laid out the night before
Thirty minutes: prayer while jogging
Burpees before the run ends

records.title: Prayer, jogging and burpees — 5:30 to 6:00
records.outcome: 13 hours of prayer and movement across the month
records.why: Thirty minutes that does two things at once: the day starts with God and with the body moving.

steps.text: The next chapter in sequence, no skipping ahead
Ten minutes: read, then sit with it
One line on what it means for today

records.title: Bible study and reflection — 6:00 to 6:10
records.why: Chapter by chapter, in sequence. Ten minutes a day covers more in a month than an occasional long sitting.

steps.text: Five minutes out loud, standing
One idea explained end to end
No filler words — pause instead

records.title: Articulation training — 6:10 to 6:15
records.why: Speaking well is trained, not inherited. Five minutes a day out loud beats an hour once a month.

steps.text: Spoken aloud, not read silently
Five minutes, no rushing the last one

records.title: Confessions and declarations — 6:15 to 6:20
records.outcome: 130 minutes of declarations spoken, not skimmed
records.why: What gets said out loud, in the first hour, sets the posture for the rest of the day.

steps.text: Yesterday in one line — what actually happened
Three priority actions for today
Name which monthly goal each one moves

records.title: Daily planning and reflection — 6:20 to 6:30
records.outcome: 26 planning sessions, each naming three priority actions
records.why: The hinge of the routine: this is where the morning turns into a day with a shape.

steps.text: Ten minutes, the current book, no switching
One note before closing it

records.title: Book reading — 6:30 to 6:40
records.outcome: 260 minutes of reading across the month
records.why: Ten minutes a day is four and a bit hours a month — a book, reliably, without ever finding time for one.

steps.text: Fifteen minutes — shower and breakfast
At the desk by 7:00

records.title: Shower and breakfast — 6:40 to 6:55
records.outcome: 26 mornings that end at the desk on time
records.why: The routine only counts if it lands you ready. Fifteen minutes, then five to move across.

records.title: Execute on the month's priorities from 7am
records.outcome: Every working day moved a monthly goal; every Sunday reviewed
records.why: The morning routine is the foundation. This is what it is a foundation for: deliberate progress, honest ownership of the outcomes, and rest taken on purpose rather than when everything is finished.

steps.text: The three priority actions come from the 6:20 planning
At least one moves a monthly goal
Done before the day fills up

records.title: Move one monthly goal, every working day
records.outcome: Meaningful progress on at least one monthly goal each working day
records.why: Three priority actions named in the morning, and at least one of them moves a goal rather than the inbox.

steps.text: One lesson or improvement, written down
Own the decision, not the circumstances

records.title: Record one lesson learned
records.outcome: 26 written entries — what I would do differently
records.why: Taking responsibility for decisions, actions and outcomes only means something if it is written down and read back.

steps.text: Read back the week
Celebrate what landed
Name what slipped, and why
Plan the week ahead

records.title: Sunday progress review
records.outcome: Four reviews a month: progress, setbacks, next week planned
records.why: Also the week's permission to stop. Breaks during the day and a proper review on Sunday are the rest side of the bargain.
